title: Phased admission + kernel steering for sustained-burst tail reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a phased admission controller combined with lightweight kernel-steering hints and attention prefetch signals to stabilize continuous batching during sustained bursty workloads. Aim is to reduce p99 tail latency for long prefill+decode requests while preserving overall throughput and keeping unit cost within current targets.

Context: Our serving runtime faces recurring p99 spikes during multi-tenant sustained bursts where prefill demand causes heterogeneous batch shapes and suboptimal kernel choices. Existing approaches (global throttles, hard slot reservations) either hurt throughput or increase cold-kernel fallbacks. This ticket proposes a three-part approach: (1) a phased admission policy that admits requests in soft waves based on backlog contour and deadline weight; (2) kernel-steering metadata (attention hint scores + expected decode length) surfaced to the admission path to bias kernel selection without forcing a hard mapping; (3) a lightweight attention-prefetch advisory that lets kernels schedule KV-cache prewarm for imminent long-sequence prefill jobs.

Goals: Reduce p99 latency for 512+ token end-to-end requests by >=20% under sustained 95th-percentile load profiles; avoid >3% throughput regression; keep error rate and OOM incidents at baseline; expose observability to track batch shapes, kernel churn, and admission rejections per-tenant.

Why different from previous work: Prior tickets optimized batching heuristics or kernel matching after slot allocation. This design moves a small set of heuristics earlier into admission, letting the system nudge admitted work toward kernels that are both performant and warm while retaining elastic batching for short requests. The kernel steering is advisory only — we prefer soft affinity to avoid tight coupling that complicates fallbacks and upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Phased admission controller implemented with configurable wave intervals and per-tenant deadline weighting exposed in runtime config
Admission layer emits kernel-hint and attention-prefetch advisory metadata to kernel selection path and scheduler
End-to-end benchmarking shows >=20% reduction in p99 latency for test workload 'sustained-burst-512-100qps' compared to baseline (same hardware, same model family)
Throughput drop <=3% and average token cost delta <=2% in the above benchmark
No increase in OOM or decode failures across 48-hour soak test; automated alerts configured for any regression
Console dashboards display batch-shape histograms, kernel churn rate, admission acceptance rate, and per-tenant tail-latency; runbook updated
Canary rollout plan and rollback mechanism validated (canary to 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%)
notes: Benchmark harness uses workload generator 'sustained-burst-512-100qps' located in infra/benchmarks/workloads
Kernel hint schema: {expected_decode_len:int, attention_hint_score:float, prefill_expected:bool} (advisory only) — schema documented in RFC
Config knobs: wave_interval_ms, wave_capacity_fraction, tenant_deadline_weight, steering_weight (0.0-1.0)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Implement phased admission controller and simple scoring function (2 weeks) — feature gated
Phase 2: Add kernel-hint metadata flow and wire into kernel selector as advisory hints (1 week)
Phase 3: Implement attention-prefetch advisory + KV prewarm path in runtime kernels (2 weeks) — conservative memory guardrails
Phase 4: Run targeted benchmarks and 48h soak on staging; iterate on steering_weight and wave_interval_ms (1 week)
Phase 5: Canary rollouts with per-canary regressions gates; monitor and roll back if p99 increases or error rate rises
tradeoffs_and_risks: Soft kernel steering reduces tail but could increase kernel churn; risk mitigated by steering_weight knob and cooldown periods
Prefetching KV caches uses GPU memory headroom — mispredictions could increase memory pressure; implement strict guardrails and global prefetch budget
Admission bounds that are too conservative harm throughput; bounds should be tuned per-cluster and per-tenant
Increased complexity in admission path may complicate future refactors; keep code paths small and well-tested
rollout_plan: Feature flag default: off in runtime-1.22, enabled behind runtime.experiments.phased_admission
Canary stage 1: 5% traffic for 24h with synthetic sustained-burst traffic and parity traffic mix
Canary stage 2: 20% traffic for 48h, expand to 2 regions, compare metrics to control cluster
Canary stage 3: 60% traffic for 48h, monitor console dashboards and automated gates
Full rollout: 100% after stability confirmed; post-release 7-day regression review
monitoring_and_gating: Primary gates: p99 latency (model-route level), admission acceptance ratio, kernel-churn rate, error rate
Hard rollback triggers: p99 regression >10% for 30m or error rate increase >0.1% absolute
Soft alarms: kernel-churn growth >50% sustained for 15m, prefetch memory budget exhaustion warnings
Dashboards: runtime -> batch-shaping -> phased-admission view (requires new panels)
benchmarks_and_results: Staging run 2026-03-05: sustained-burst-512-100qps baseline p99=482ms; with phased admission + steering p99=372ms (22.8% reduction)
Token cost: baseline $0.01357/1k tokens; experiment $0.01347/1k tokens (-0.7%)
Soak test 24h with canary flags on staging: no OOMs, one transient kernel-fallback recorded (investigated, benign)
next_steps: Address kernel-fallback diagnostic: add more logging when steering hint mismatch triggers fallback
Tune steering_weight per HW class (A100 vs H100) based on upcoming perf jobs
Add tenant-level admission telemetry to detect noisy neighbors and add mitigations
Prepare PRs for runtime and kernel repos and link them in this ticket before review
